subject: Pilot & Commercial Path: usage definitions, price protection, and true-up
messages:
From: Sara Thompson <sara@finlytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@finlytics.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Interest in pilot — need clarity on MAP milestones & commercial guardrails
Attachments: Finlytics-MAP-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the latency/cost numbers you showed are compelling. Our team wants to move from evaluation to a 30-day pilot, but procurement and engineering have flagged a few commercial items we need clarified before we can commit:

- Usage definitions: we need explicit language about what counts toward billed "generation tokens" vs "embedding units" and how batch/async inference is measured.
- Price protection / increases: procurement wants a mechanism to avoid sudden price changes between pilot and production.
- True-up cadence: do you do quarterly or annual true-ups for overage vs committed units?
- Escrow/KMS: our security team asked whether escrow for model weights or an HSM/KMS integration is required for a pilot.

I've attached a rough MAP sketch our internal team put together; it's lightweight but shows the milestones we care about (pilot acceptance, ramp to 100k tokens/day, production go-live). Can we align on a short mutual action plan and a clean set of redlines so procurement can issue a PO?

Can you and your legal ops provide suggested language for: price protection, a true-up waterfall, and a clear definition of "Normalized Usage" we can insert into the SOW?

Regards,
Sara
Sara Thompson
Head of AI Platform — Finlytics

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@finlytics.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mchen@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interest in pilot — need clarity on MAP milestones & commercial guardrails
Attachments: redwood_map_template_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Hi Sara — really appreciate the clear MAP sketch. Happy to get this moving. High level proposal from Redwood to unblock pilot:

1) Pilot (30 days): single-team access, up to 50k generation tokens/day and 5k embedding units/day (no charge overage during pilot; we log usage).
2) Ramp window (60 days after pilot acceptance): target 100k gen tokens/day, with a staged commit path: 0–100k, 100k–300k, >300k (pricing tiers attached).
3) Price protection: we can offer a 12-month price protection window on committed unit pricing post-signature. Increases outside of that window limited to CPI but capped at 6% annually.
4) True-up: for committed contracts we prefer quarterly true-ups to keep billing timely; happy to discuss annual true-up if that is strictly required by procurement.
5) Usage definitions: attaching our MAP template with an SOW appendix that defines Generation Token, Embedding Unit, Batch Request, and Async Job. We can also include a clause for "Normalized Usage" to strip dev/test spikes from true-ups.

On escrow/KMS: for the pilot, escrow of model weights is typically not necessary. We can offer customer-managed keys (KMS) for data-at-rest and integrate with your HSM for production if needed.

Next steps: I'll loop in our commercial counsel to draft concise redlines on price protection/true-up language. Can we do a 30-minute sync this week to finalize the MAP? Proposed times: Wed 8/31 10:00 or Thu 9/1 14:00 PT.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Stephanie — quick follow from procurement/IT: a few clarifications we need before procurement signs PO:

- Price protection detail: the 12-month window is good; we need to add a "price change notification" period (60 days) and a one-time right to terminate or renegotiate if increases exceed 4% annually.
- True-up cadence: procurement favors annual true-ups to align with our financial calendar. Quarterly is difficult for our AP process.
- Usage definitions: importantly, API-level retries and async replays should not double-bill us. We need explicit examples in the SOW.
- Escrow: model-weights escrow is not required. KMS integration for keys is preferred for production; for pilot, dev keys are ok.

If you can provide sample contract language (we can redline) that covers "Normalized Usage" and a practical true-up workflow, we can push the PO through next week.

Thanks,
Mark
Director of Procurement — Finlytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Finlytics — negotiation points & proposed playbook
Attachments: pricing-protection-draft.txt (text/plain)

Folks — looping you in. Key negotiation posture I suggest (short bullets):

- Pilot: no overage billing, observing only. Keeps procurement comfortable and shortens cycle.
- Price protection: we offer 12 months post-signature with 60-day notice; push back on the 4% hard cap — propose CPI with a 6% absolute cap.
- True-up: offer both options — quarterly preferred by us; annual acceptable if they take a shorter price-protection window (e.g., 9 months) or agree to an interim invoice mechanism handled via AP.
- Usage defs: include explicit API examples and a "retry dedupe" clause that excludes server-side retries from billing.
- Escrow: decline model-weights escrow; offer KMS/HSM integration for production and a SOC2 evidence package for pilot.

Attached is a short draft clause for price-protection + true-up. Neha — can you produce redline language that covers normalized usage and a fallback for model-variant routing if capacity or pricing changes are needed?

–Ben

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Finlytics — negotiation points & proposed playbook
Attachments: redlines_finlytics_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks Ben — drafted a concise set of redlines. Summary of proposed legal language (high level):

1) Definitions (SOW Appendix A):
- "Generation Tokens": characters/bytes consumed by model generation as measured by the API server at the time of request.
- "Embedding Units": billed per 1,000 vectors returned; batching normalization applies (see batching rule).
- "Normalized Usage": calculated by excluding (i) test/dev environments identified by IP ranges and API keys provided at execution, (ii) automated retries resulting in identical request IDs, and (iii) anomalous spikes where usage exceeds 5x daily median for three consecutive days.

2) Price Protection Clause:
- Committed Unit prices are fixed for a 12-month period post-signature. Price changes thereafter require 60 days' notice and may not exceed CPI + 3% but in absolute terms capped at 6% annually.

3) True-up and Billing:
- Default true-up cadence: quarterly invoicing with aggregated usage statements.
- Alternative: if customer requires annual true-up, an interim pro forma invoice will be issued each quarter to align operationally; final settlement annually.

4) Escrow / Key Management:
- Escrow of model weights: expressly declined for hosted models.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood will support customer-managed keys for data-at-rest and provide a SOC2 attestation package for pilot.

5) Model Variant Fallback:
- Customer may request fallback to a functionally-compatible model variant if primary model is unavailable; pricing for fallback shall be the same or lower.

I've attached detailed redline language in the doc. If the team is comfortable with these items, I recommend sending to Finlytics with Ben's commercial play and a 30-minute sign-off sync.

Neha Kapoor
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Stephanie/Ben/Neha — thanks for the quick turnaround and the helpful redlines. Procurement reviewed Neha's language and Ben's playbook; we can accept the following and move forward:

- 30-day pilot as proposed; no overage billing during pilot.
- 12-month price protection on committed unit pricing with 60-day notice; Finlytics requests a one-time right to renegotiate if the annual increase exceeds 5% — we accept the CPI + 3% formula if you can bring the absolute cap down to 5% for this account.
- We'll take the annual true-up option aligned to our fiscal year, with Redwood issuing interim pro forma invoices quarterly for operational reconciliation.
- Normalized Usage definition looks good; we'll supply dev/test IP ranges and API keys for exclusion.
- Escrow not required; we request documentation for KMS integration during production onboarding.

Attached is the PO stub; this is contingent on final redlined SOW and a short MAP (pilot acceptance criteria + ramp milestones) that we can sign electronically.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to share final SOW + MAP redlines by Mon 9/6.
2) We sign the MAP, procurement issues final PO.
3) Pilot begins within 7 business days of PO.

Thanks — excited to get started.

Regards,
Sara
